AI-written by Codex, reading alone on 22 November 2026. Source snapshot `5a4f546e6fae82bc0555266bc946ac4280c4b066`. Every call and line gain below is on paper. No Lean was written to a module, run, or built.

#### OPENED — A · The first exceptional index on a finite prefix

OPENED — F is exactly ReadOffInTime:196, moved with its public name. It is constructive even when P and Q overlap. Its witness carries Q and a prefix of P. Calling that the first Q requires disjointness. B is the strict-end adapter below. It calls F once. Its six source lines, including its new signature, are charged here. A global DecidablePred is stronger than this proof needs. Only the visited points need the displayed disjunction, and none of the calls converts a proof of an Or into a data-valued Decidable instance.

```text
B {P Q : Nat → Prop} (d : ∀ t, P t ∨ Q t) (n : Nat) :
    (∀ t, t < n → P t) ∨ ∃ m, m < n ∧ Q m ∧ ∀ t, t < m → P t :=
  (F d n).elim (fun all => .inl fun t lt => all t (Nat.le_of_lt lt))
    fun ⟨m, le, q, pre⟩ => (Nat.lt_or_eq_of_le le).elim
      (fun lt => .inr ⟨m, lt, q, pre⟩)
      (fun same => .inl (same ▸ pre))
```

In the paper terms below, trim is the literal lambda `fun ⟨i, h, q, _⟩ => ⟨i, h, q⟩`, em abbreviates Decidable.em, and swap is Or.symm. Each expands on its line. F and B keep the original statement of every replaced row. The two Optimum neighbors have different proof status. Only one contains the long first-fall induction. The five-line neighbor can itself use F. Optimum's start is necessary for the stronger conclusion at the first fall. Frequency's LPO supplies decisions of whole rows. It cannot be deleted without replacement.

Stock uses Amounts:506 as its interval adapter. That particular theorem is about P alone, so move it as well to Prelude, keeping its namespace. GrammarLaws uses the next family’s L. Its own count and list-split lemmas then drop out of this proof. The bounded hypothesis N and k < N in Likeness:1722 go unused. Store the public statement unchanged or offer a separate weaker caller. No assumption that every t decides P is manufactured in Decidedness:148 or Presence:618.

```text
DR {α : Type u} {R : α → α → Prop} (refl : ∀ x, R x x) :
    ∀ {s : List α}, DistinctUnder R s → Distinct s
  | [], _ => trivial
  | a :: _, ⟨fresh,h⟩ =>
    ⟨fun m => fresh a m (refl a), DR refl h⟩
```

#### OPENED — O · Branching tests on listed outcomes

OPENED — In this module the unqualified FiniteDecided results use a list of *all* states and decisions of transitions. OutcomesListed supplies just the list relevant to a move. Its decisions of realized claims are the same. A positive listing of the outcomes can be built under an existential in Prop, even if the step decisions themselves are only in Prop. No Decidable instance, DecidableEq, or choice function is available. The conversion below is the cost of reusing the later group, including the two long inductions. Move the existing OutcomesListed declarations to precede their uses, after the shared AlikeTo, BranchingTest and decision facts. Move Likeness:1804 Decided.forall_in before this block too. Decided.exists_not_in already comes from Decidedness. Keep the module's other later theorems in place. No theorem about all horizons, and no omniscience principle, is needed here.

Use V and X as the paper names of just these two adapters. V also gives the bridge between the two BranchingTest list theorems. The 19 lines below include the signatures.

```text
V {A : Type u} (q : A → Prop) (d : ∀ a, Decided (q a)) :
    ∀ l : List A, ∃ w : List A, ∀ x, x ∈ w ↔ x ∈ l ∧ q x
  | [] => ⟨[], fun _ => ⟨fun m => nomatch m, And.left⟩⟩
  | a::l => match V q d l with
    | ⟨w,h⟩ => match d a with
      | .inl yes => ⟨a::w, fun x => ⟨fun m => (mem_cons_cases m).elim
          (fun e => ⟨e.symm ▸ List.Mem.head l,e.symm ▸ yes⟩)
          (fun mw => ⟨.tail a ((h x).mp mw).1,((h x).mp mw).2⟩),
        fun ⟨m,p⟩ => (mem_cons_cases m).elim (fun e => e.symm ▸ List.Mem.head w)
          (fun ml => .tail a ((h x).mpr ⟨ml,p⟩))⟩⟩
      | .inr no => ⟨w, fun x => ⟨fun mw => ⟨.tail a ((h x).mp mw).1,((h x).mp mw).2⟩,
        fun ⟨m,p⟩ => (mem_cons_cases m).elim (fun e => (no (e ▸ p)).elim)
          (fun ml => (h x).mpr ⟨ml,p⟩)⟩⟩
X {F : Frame S A C} (f : FiniteDecided F) : OutcomesListed F :=
  ⟨fun s a => match f.listed with
    | ⟨l,all⟩ => match V (F.P.step s a) (f.step s a) l with
      | ⟨w,h⟩ => ⟨w, fun t => ⟨fun p => (h t).mpr ⟨all t,p⟩,
          fun m => ((h t).mp m).2⟩⟩,
   f.realized⟩
```
 Decidedness:476 is a constructive filter with a count, but its α is only Type 0 (the section variable at :95). The two frames and apart_from_listed quantify over arbitrary universes. A direct call there would narrow the old result.

```text
AnyOn {α : Type u} {p q : α → Bool}
    {l : List α} (same : ∀ x, x ∈ l → p x = q x) :
    l.any p = l.any q := match l, same with
  | [], _ => rfl
  | a :: l, h => by
    show (p a || l.any p) = (q a || l.any q)
    rw [h a (.head l), AnyOn (l := l) fun x m => h x (.tail a m)]
``` For List.all the existing membership-restricted theorem has the needed small universe already. Move FaultEnvelopes:149 to Prelude.

J takes a world W, the original free hypothesis, and the sevenfold conjunction in Counting:264 with W substituted for queue n c. Its conclusion is W.Meets S. Its 10-line body is exactly :748 with the first line replaced by “match seven with”. The new signature, wrapped into four lines plus the ten proof lines, is charged below. Counting and Standing already have the direct import link.

```text
J (W : World) {S : Premise → Bool} (free : S .embodied = false)
    (seven : W.Dependent ∧ W.Balanced ∧ W.Acting ∧ W.Taking ∧
      W.Dissipative ∧ W.Counted ∧ W.Transmitting) :
    W.Meets S :=
  match seven with
  | ⟨dependent, balanced, acting, taking, dissipative, counted, transmitting⟩ => fun
    | .dependent, _ => dependent
    | .balanced, _ => balanced
    | .acting, _ => acting
    | .taking, _ => taking
    | .dissipative, _ => dissipative
    | .embodied, selected => nomatch free.symm.trans selected
    | .counted, _ => counted
    | .transmitting, _ => transmitting
```

#### OPENED — AQ · The first successful entry in a list, with its computed result

OPENED — Prelude’s list search supplies both membership and truth of the computed hit; find_none_iff supplies existence when a qualifying entry is known. Parting:531 runs precisely the Boolean test q y := live P moves all all.length y. Identification:673 uses its explicit family of decision instances. Its Boolean test is b x := @decide (p x) (dec x). These are named Option-valued functions: a bare existential from each_or_some would discard a required equation. The two conversion proofs below keep both existing recursive functions in place, including their reduction rules. Barring qualification, FF p dec l and FL l are the two equations in the directions shown. HIT consumes a listed x and a proof its Boolean test returns true. This is a positive case of seed (f), separate from leading_exact. The equation at the named result is what makes it work.

```text
HIT {α : Type u} {q : α → Bool} {l : List α} {x : α} (m : x ∈ l) (yes : q x = true) :
    ∃ b, l.find? q = some b := match e : l.find? q with
  | some b => ⟨b,rfl⟩
  | none => False.elim (Bool.noConfusion (((ListTests.find_none_iff.mp e) x m).symm.trans yes))
FL : ∀ l, firstLive P moves all l = l.find? q
  | [] => rfl
  | x::l => by
    change cond (q x) (some x) (firstLive P moves all l) =
      (match q x with | true => some x | false => l.find? q)
    cases q x <;> first | exact FL l | rfl
FF (p : α → Prop) (dec : ∀ x, Decidable (p x)) : ∀ l, firstFit p dec l = l.find? b
  | [] => rfl
  | x::l => by
    change (if p x then some x else firstFit p dec l) =
      (match b x with | true => some x | false => l.find? b)
    cases dec x with
    | isTrue h => rw [if_pos h, (show b x = true from @decide_eq_true (p x) (dec x) h)]
    | isFalse h => rw [if_neg h, (show b x = false from @decide_eq_false (p x) (dec x) h)]
                   exact FF p dec l
``` In FF, b is syntactic shorthand for the local test with its explicit dec. In FL, q similarly expands to the actual live test. HIT can sit after find_none_iff in Prelude; FL and FF remain beside their own definitions, so no owner-to-owner import is proposed. Verification would have to check the reduction of List.find? at cons and the explicit decision instance in FF; zero import growth does not check either equation.

The formal links gained are theorem calls, including LineOnAStock → Identification, EventualWidening’s Web theorem → Reaching’s chain, and the earlier Likeness theorem → OutcomesListed. The proposals do not require a new peer-to-peer module dependency. Moving a pure proof down can give it two callers even when adding the old owner as an import would cycle.

OPENED — The normalized-text groups follow the worked ranking as a separate tied tier with zero *credited* gain. M2 and M4 are recorded wherever the printed size or date settles them. For many of these groups the available comparison leaves M1, M3 and M5 open.

#### OPENED — 1. Finite choice, search and double negation

OPENED — A selected list of pairs with map Prod.fst = l records a witness in the right position for *each occurrence*. The continuation at gather_listed supplies propositions to a final consumer. M1 for substituting the three listed theorems for each other.

#### OPENED — 2. First witness, a computed cutoff, and least score

OPENED — An arbitrary yes/no sequence can be true, false, true. <a id="proof-register"></a>

### OPENED — Whole-package proof-text comparison

OPENED — I stripped nested block and line comments, indexed theorem headers and proof bodies, preserved numerals, punctuation, selected control syntax and the equality pattern of recurring identifiers, assigned identifiers successive numbers, and gave recursive self references a separate token. I ran a second comparison that protected field names and known declaration names. The broad register below contains every repeated normalized body from the first pass. Groups with at least one case or recursion marker come first; markers include pattern lambdas, eliminators, and ifs. The remaining groups are included under the literal reading of Q1(g), including proof terms as short as rfl. There was no minimum line cutoff. It includes 395 groups with a marker and 574 without. The narrower field/name-preserving pass produced 486 repeated forms with 2,048 entries. It prioritized inspection; the register retains the broader matches. Normalization leaves whitespace at token boundaries, so differently spaced but otherwise identical terms can still miss each other. A repeated script is evidence for a repeated proof shape. It does not establish name resolution, reducibility, universes, constructor correspondence, or a reusable theorem. First-occurrence renaming can replace constants and identifier-shaped text inside strings. Alternative one-line projections and the same tactic with different instances also occur. Conversely, it can miss equivalent proofs written with different eliminators, binder syntax or branch order. For each group I give the declarations, dates, proof lengths and shared import boundary. Where no term was derived I retain its proof in the ledger, leave its semantic status open, and count zero prospective savings. This avoids reporting all case tables about different concrete worlds as formal joins.
